hero.eyebrow: Digital skills from zero · Nothing to install
hero.title: Basic Computer & Internet Literacy
hero.subtitle: Learn how computers and the internet work, manage files, search, email, and stay safe from scams and weak passwords, with practice labs that check your work.
hero.outcomeLine: After this course you can use a computer and the internet confidently, and protect yourself and your family.

outcomes.title: Know your device
outcomes.text: Parts of a computer, software, storage and what slows a device down.

outcomes.title: Manage files
outcomes.text: Folders, file names, copy, cut, paste and the shortcuts that save time.

outcomes.title: Use the web well
outcomes.text: Browsers, web addresses, searching and judging what you find.

outcomes.title: Communicate clearly
outcomes.text: Write good emails, share files safely and behave well online.

outcomes.title: Stay safe
outcomes.text: Strong passwords, 2-step verification, scams, updates and backups.

outcomes.title: Handle daily tasks
outcomes.text: Pay and fill in forms safely, fix problems and keep learning.

assessment: Finish the required labs in each module: they are checked automatically and explained when something is missing.
Pass each module quiz (70% or more). You can retry as often as you like.
Complete the final project and the final assessment to finish the course.

faq.a: No. The course starts from the very beginning and explains every word it uses.

faq.q: Does it matter whether I use Windows, a Mac or a phone?
faq.a: The ideas are the same everywhere. Where a shortcut differs, the lesson shows the Windows and Mac versions.
About twelve hours, in short sessions. Each module takes around two hours.
Finishing every module and the final assessment marks the course complete on your Yugty profile.

activities.title: How many photos fit on a phone?
activities.objective: Use storage units (MB and GB) and a formula to estimate how much will fit.
activities.scenario: A phone has 64 GB of storage. One photo takes about 4 MB, one minute of video takes about 100 MB, and the system and apps already use 20 GB. How many photos could you still store?
steps: In B4 work out the free storage in GB: total minus used.
In B5 change the free storage into MB (1 GB is 1,024 MB).
In B6 find how many photos fit: free MB divided by the size of one photo.
In B7 find how many minutes of video would fit in the same space.

checks.label: B4 is 44 GB free
checks.explain: Free space is what is left after the used part.

checks.label: B5 is 45,056 MB
checks.explain: 1 GB is 1,024 MB, so multiply by 1,024.

checks.label: B6 is 11,264 photos
checks.explain: Free MB divided by the MB one photo takes.

checks.label: B7 is about 450 minutes of video
checks.explain: Use the video minute size in D3: 45,056 divided by 100, about 450 minutes.

checks.label: No error messages
checks.hint: Check that every formula points at the right cell.
checks.explain: A clean sheet has no error codes.

activities.title: Write better searches
activities.objective: Turn vague searches into specific ones and record why each is better.
activities.scenario: A good search uses the words a good page would contain. Rewrite four vague searches so they are more likely to find what you want, and list them.
steps: Write a title as a heading.
Make a numbered list of at least four rewritten searches.
After the list, write a paragraph of at least 25 words saying what you changed and why.
Put at least one search inside quotation marks.

activities.title: Write a clear, polite email
activities.objective: Write an email with a subject line, a greeting, a short body, a clear request and a closing.
activities.scenario: You need to ask your teacher, Mr Rao, for an extra day to hand in a project because you were ill. Write the email.
steps: Write a subject line starting with the word Subject: and make it specific.
Greet Mr Rao by name.
Write a short body (at least 30 words) that explains the reason and says exactly what you are asking for.
Thank him and sign off with your name.

checks.label: A subject line

checks.explain: A greeting is polite and shows who the email is for.

checks.label: A body of at least 30 words

checks.explain: A polite closing finishes the email well.

activities.title: Scam or genuine?
activities.objective: Spot the signs of a scam message and the signs of a genuine one.
activities.scenario: Scammers use phone calls, texts and emails that look official. Real organisations behave differently. Decide which of these are scam signs and which are normal.
steps: Read each message or request.
Choose Scam sign or Looks genuine.

activities.title: Capstone: a digital safety card for your family
activities.objective: Combine what you have learned into one clear, usable card.
activities.scenario: Make a one-page card you could give your family, with simple rules for staying safe online.
steps: A title as a heading and a short introduction of at least 25 words.
A heading called Passwords with a bulleted list of at least three rules.
A heading called Scams with a bulleted list of at least three warning signs.
A heading called If something goes wrong with a numbered list of at least three steps.
Bold the single most important rule.

checks.label: A title heading
checks.hint: Apply a heading style to the title.
checks.explain: The title says what the card is.

checks.label: An introduction of at least 25 words
checks.hint: Say who the card is for and why it matters.
checks.explain: A short introduction gives the reason to read.

checks.label: At least four headings
checks.hint: Use headings for Passwords, Scams and If something goes wrong, plus the title.
checks.explain: Headings make the card quick to use.

checks.label: A bulleted list
checks.hint: Use bullet lists for the rules and warning signs.
checks.explain: Lists are quick to scan.

checks.label: A numbered list of steps
checks.hint: Use a numbered list for what to do when something goes wrong.

checks.label: It mentions never sharing an OTP or PIN
checks.hint: Include a rule about never sharing an OTP, PIN or password.
checks.explain: This is the rule scammers most want people to break.

checks.label: The most important rule is bold
checks.hint: Select it and press B.
checks.explain: Bold shows what matters most.
